correctness.rationale: For the stated positive deterministic scalar SIS domain, global nonnegative invariance and a finite monotone gain are proved directly; square integrability plus bounded derivative forces infection to zero. Before crossing the static threshold, the exact homogeneous quadratic change y=beta/delta-g, z=\(x/y\) and positive time reparameterization yields \(dz/d\tau=z(\delta-\beta z+\alpha z^2)\). The discriminant and initial-ratio tests determine whether z converges to a finite root or diverges. Bounded z gives exact \(1/t\) constants via \(d(1/y)/dt=\alpha z^2\); unbounded z gives finite physical crossing time because x remains positive, forcing strict gain overshoot and exponential decay. Exact rational side tests and direct ODE simulations pass 300228 assertions but are not used for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 full-length primary model supplies extinction and finite limiting gains but not the sharp quadratic recovery-gain spectral margin, seed-dependent separatrix, or 1/t coefficients. The 2025 indexed journal material discusses power-dependent behavior without this result. Six actual semantic record queries and targeted public article searches identified related relaxation and control papers with different systems or weaker coverage. Accessible earlier scientific claims were checked for overlap. This supports best-knowledge originality, not global priority proof. A relevant journal PDF could not be read and remains a named risk.

value.rationale: The natural quadratic-member recovery controller had proven eventual eradication but no precise distinction between just-critical reproduction-one control and subcritical exponential elimination. This full parameter-and-initial-state classification supplies an explicit sharp adaptation-rate boundary, seed separatrix, equality-ray solution and physical-time decay constants. The same baseline/adaptation rates can yield different long-time margins for different initial infection fractions, a nontrivial policy-control distinction. Claims are limited to the scalar deterministic model; no broader network theorem is asserted.
